                                     PROJECT NO. 58481


 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                         §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                      §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA 37.0561                    §                   OF TEXAS


    AEP TEXAS INC.’S COMMENTS ON STAFF’S SECOND DISCUSSION DRAFT

       AEP Texas Inc. (AEP Texas) respectfully submits these comments in response to Public

Utility of Texas Commission (Commission) Staff’s January 2, 2026 2 nd Discussion Draft regarding

large load interconnection standards under PURA § 37.0561 and the discussion at the January 9,

2026 Workshop. AEP Texas appreciates Staff’s continued work on the rulemaking and the

opportunity to provide comments. An Executive Summary of AEP Texas’ comments is provided

at the conclusion of its comments.

                                             COMMENTS

Definition of Interconnection Agreement

       AEP Texas requests that the definition of interconnection agreement be revised to remove

‘securitized’ and instead include ‘financial commitment’ because security and CIAC are being

collected during this agreement.

       (7)     Interconnection agreement -- An agreement, executed and securitized with
               financial commitment by a large load customer and interconnecting utility after
               completion of all necessary transmission studies, that, at a minimum, satisfies
               subsection (i) of this section.

Initial Screening Study

       AEP Texas recommends that the proposed initial screening study timeline be changed to

45 days, instead of the 30 days currently in the 2nd Discussion Draft, as additional time is needed

to study and scope the direct connection of the Customer. The extra time is needed because without
 the scope, there will not be any details available on the timeline of the direct connection. AEP

Texas also requests that the Commission revise the language in Section (d) (1) to include ‘direct

connect’ before interconnection timeline. This addition will provide clarity that at this stage there

will not be an understanding of the direct connect and any system upgrades that may be necessary

but just the direct connect portion.

(d)     Initial screening study. Not later than 45 30 days after receipt of the disclosures and study
        fee required under subsection (c) of this section, the interconnecting utility must complete
        an initial screening study if requested by the large load customer.

        (1)     If, based on the initial screening study, the interconnecting utility provides the large
                load customer with a direct connect interconnection timeline of three years or more,
                the large load customer may:

Large Load Interconnection Study

        AEP Texas suggests that the timeline for the initiation of the LLIS process begin no later

than 90 days after the receipt of the disclosures and study fee to allow for the time needed to sign

the intermediate agreement prior, instead of the 60 days currently included in the 2 nd Discussion

Draft. This will ensure that the security is received and the agreement is signed, preventing the

queue from continuing to be inundated with LLIS requests that are not ready to move forward. The

addition of the word ‘process’ to the provision is to provide clarity of when in the process timeline

the language was referencing.

        (e)      Large load interconnection study. Not later than 60 90 days after receipt of the
        disclosures and study fee required under subsection (c) of this section, the interconnecting
        utility must coordinate with ERCOT to scope and initiate a large load interconnection study
        process.



Intermediate Agreement

        AEP Texas suggests that this provision be revised to reflect that the agreement should be

signed prior to moving into the LLIS queue.


Project No. 54841                                  2                            AEP Texas, Inc. Comments
 (f)         Intermediate agreement. Before a large load interconnection study is begun initiated, the
            large load customer must execute and securitize an intermediate agreement that, at a
            minimum, includes the updated disclosures and financial commitments under this
            subsection. The interconnecting utility must cancel the interconnection request and notify
            ERCOT of the cancellation if the large load customer fails to execute and securitize an
            intermediate agreement within 30 days of the commencement of the large load
            interconnection study.

Interconnection agreement

            AEP Texas currently requires its Letter of Agreement (LOA) to be signed within 90 days.

The proposal in the 2nd Discussion Draft to allow 180 days to pass after studies are completed can

create a situation where the studies become stale. Studies becoming stale is one of the complaints

of the existing process because it drives re-studies.

      (i)      Interconnection agreement. Not later than 180 90 days after completion of the large
               load interconnection study for a large load customer, the large load customer must
               execute and securitize with financial commitment an interconnection agreement with
               the interconnecting utility that, at a minimum, includes the updated disclosures and
               financial commitments under this subsection. The interconnecting utility must cancel
               the interconnection request and notify ERCOT of the cancellation if the large load
               customer fails to execute and securitize an interconnection agreement under this
               subsection within 180 days of receipt of the interconnecting utility’s notice that the
               interconnecting utility and ERCOT have completed all necessary transmission studies
               to interconnect the large load customer.

Financial security for significant equipment and services

            AEP Texas suggests removing the phrase ‘and services’. It is unclear what services would

have a 6-month lead time and the descriptions found under this all section of the rule are all related

to the equipment.

            (8) Financial security for significant equipment and services. An interconnecting
            utility must not procure equipment before a large load customer pays financial security to
            the interconnecting utility in an amount equal to the interconnecting utility’s estimated
            costs for equipment with a lead time of at least six months and services necessary to
            interconnect the large load customer.




Project No. 54841                                    3                          AEP Texas, Inc. Comments
 Contribution in Aid of Construction

        AEP Texas is concerned that there may be a potential impact with the current description

in this section. In the past, AEP Texas structured the CIAC into payments that alignment with the

construction schedule per customer requests. The proposed change could significantly impact a

customer who cannot fully fund upfront costs for construction. Within the same section, the

language included is for studying a load individually; When AEP Texas continues the process of

looking at loads statewide, it will be difficult to accomplish section (B) as currently included in

the 2nd Discussion Draft.

Withdrawal of all or a portion of requested or contracted peak demand for interconnection

        AEP Texas proposes a revision to prevent a load from changing requirements throughout

the process. This would become burdensome in the amount of communication, documentation,

and the initial screening study or Large Load Interconnection Studies.

                (j) Withdrawal of all or a portion of requested or contracted peak demand
                for interconnection. A large load customer may withdraw all or a portion of its -
                requested or contracted peak demand for interconnection by submitting its request
                in writing to the interconnecting utility.

        Also, within this section, and addressed at the Workshop, there is a need to extend the time

for the days to refund the remaining balance. This is due to the length of time it could take based

off of where a customer is in the process. The refund will take place as soon as possible but later

on in the process there is more work that may need to be done.

                       (B)    After applying financial security and CIAC that the large load
                       customer paid to any outstanding amounts owed, the interconnecting utility
                       must refund the remaining balance to the large load customer within 60 90
                       days.

        For consistency with the revision requested above, this revision below is also proposed.




Project No. 54841                                4                           AEP Texas, Inc. Comments
 (k)     Reallocation of capacity. An interconnecting utility must notify ERCOT of non-utilized
        capacity of a large load customer that is energized and fails to satisfy, within 18 months, a
        milestone in its schedule for phased energization of the contracted peak demand. ERCOT
        must reallocate the non-utilized capacity and the interconnecting electric utility must
        refund the balance of the large load customer’s financial security not later than 60 90 days
        after drawing down for outstanding amounts owed. Outstanding amounts owed include
        the following:

Terms for refund of financial security for a large load customer that energizes.

        AEP Texas believes that a revision to the section that adds ‘from system upgrades’ provides

clarity that the refund is not from the direct connect balance but only the system upgrades.

        (2)     The interconnecting utility must refund any remaining balance from system
                upgrades when the large load customer sustains operations for five years at the
                customer’s contracted peak demand.



                                         CONCLUSION
        AEP Texas appreciates the opportunity to provide comments in this proceeding and looks

forward to further engagement with Staff and stakeholders as the rules continue through the

drafting process.


                                                        Respectfully submitted,

     UNDER PURA 37.0561

                        AEP TEXAS INC.’S EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

       AEP Texas Inc. provides the following Executive Summary to its comments on Staff’s 2 nd
Discussion Draft filed January 2, 2026 regarding the large load interconnection standards under
PURA § 37.0561 and the discussion during the January 9, 2026 Workshop.

               AEP Texas suggests several revisions to the 2nd Discussion Draft to adjust deadlines
                to better align with processes that occur during interconnection.
               AEP Texas also suggests several revisions to sections to clarify the meaning of the
                provisions and reduce confusion.
